title: 3Sum
statement: Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets in nums that add up to zero. The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
constraints: Only unique triplets are allowed in the answer

examples.explanation: -1 + -1 + 2 = 0 and -1 + 0 + 1 = 0. The duplicate -1 pair appears only once.
No three elements sum to zero.

hints.content: The first element must be fixed before the other two can be searched for. What search finds two numbers summing to a target in a sorted array?
Sort the array first. Then for each fixed first element, the remaining two can be found with two pointers.
After sorting, for a fixed first value the target for the pair is negative of that value. Walk left and right inward from the rest of the array.

sort(nums)
for i in range(n - 2):
    if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
    left = i + 1
    right = n - 1
    while left < right:
        sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]
        if sum == 0: record; left++; right--; skip duplicates
        elif sum < 0: left++
        else: right--
Two de-duplication rules are required: skip a first element equal to the previous one, and after recording a triplet move both pointers past duplicates.

pseudocode: for each index i from 0 to n - 3:
skip i if nums[i] equals nums[i - 1]
record triplet, skip duplicate values on both pointers
invariant: For a fixed first element, moving left forward can only increase the sum and moving right backward can only decrease it, so a discarded pair can never be the answer.
whyThisPattern: Two pointers work on sorted data because order tells you which direction to move. Sorting converts the array into a structure where each comparison eliminates half of the remaining candidates, and the outer loop fixes the first element so the inner search becomes the classic pair problem.
bruteForce: Three nested loops: O(n^3). At n = 10,000 that is about 10^12 operations. Sorting plus two pointers reduces the inner work from n to n while keeping the outer loop, so the total is O(n^2).
interviewExplanation: I sort the array, then fix the first element and search for the other two with two pointers moving inward from both ends. If the total is too small I move left forward, and if it is too large I move right backward, which is correct because the array is sorted. I also skip duplicate values so each unique triplet is produced once, giving O(n^2) time.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to skip a repeated first element, which produces duplicate triplets.
Moving only one pointer after recording a triplet, which produces duplicates.
Trying to run two pointers on the unsorted array, where the direction rules no longer hold.

animationSteps.description: Two pointers need order to decide a direction.
animationSteps.text: After sorting the array is -4, -1, -1, 0, 1, 2, so moving right backward always reduces the sum.

animationSteps.title: Fix the first element
animationSteps.description: i = 0 with value -4, the pair target becomes 4.
animationSteps.text: First element -4 at index 0, left pointer at index 1 with -1, right pointer at index 5 with 2. The total is -3, too small.

animationSteps.title: Predict the move
animationSteps.description: The total is -3, which is less than 0.
animationSteps.text: The running total is -3 and the target is 0. Choose which pointer moves next.

payload.explanation: Moving left forward is the only way to raise the sum, because the array is sorted.

animationSteps.title: Left advances
animationSteps.description: Left moves to the second -1, total becomes -3 again.
animationSteps.text: Left moves to index 2 holding -1. The total is still -3, so the duplicate value at the same position tells us to keep moving left.

animationSteps.title: First triplet found
animationSteps.text: First element -1 at index 1, left -1 at index 2, right 2 at index 5. The total is -1 plus -1 plus 2 which is 0, so the triplet [-1, -1, 2] is recorded.

animationSteps.title: Unique triplets only
animationSteps.text: The result is [-1, -1, 2] and [-1, 0, 1]. Duplicate values are skipped on the first element and on both pointers.

payload.message: Two unique triplets returned in O(n^2) time.
